questions.prompt: Canva's best-practice page says when to use a brand template and autofill. When?

options.text: When you need a brand new concept or creative direction
options.explanation: The Canva docs say to use generation for that.

options.text: When you need consistent, repeatable output from prepared content
options.explanation: Right. The layout is fixed and only the data changes.

options.text: When the design has legal rules a generated asset may break
options.explanation: For that, the Canva docs say to use user-provided, approved assets.

questions.prompt: What does Adobe's Data Merge API take in to make its variations?

options.text: A text prompt and a style image
options.explanation: That is a generation job, not a data merge.

options.text: A template document and a CSV file
options.explanation: Right. The Adobe Firefly docs say data merge generates variations of a template document from data in a CSV file.
Brand template IDs belong to Canva. Data Merge uses an InDesign file.

questions.prompt: What does update_in_place do on Canva's autofill-design tool?

options.text: It makes a safe copy first, then fills the copy
options.explanation: It does the opposite: it replaces the existing design's content.

options.text: It replaces the content, and it can't be undone
options.explanation: Right. The Canva docs say to set it only when the user explicitly asks to refill that design.

options.text: It only changes the title and the folder name
options.explanation: It replaces the content, not only the title.
